Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Stuffing the paper into the cup
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Paper is stuffed into the cup.
node.criteria: Return yes when support 1 passes: the requested outcome is visibly complete. Return no only when support 1 fails and support 2 fails, establishing that no requested change has progressed. Return partial when support 1 fails and support 2 passes, establishing some progress without completion. Return unknown whenever the evidence needed to distinguish these alternatives is unresolved. A skipped support is unobserved, not automatically inapplicable; on any skipped path, return a decision only if the remaining evidence establishes that same outcome under the rubric, otherwise return unknown. Supporting evidence earns no completion credit independently, and unrelated edits do not count as progress.
node.binding: Target: The paper is visibly placed inside the cup, with evidence that it has been stuffed into it rather than merely resting nearby or on its rim.. Reference: The requested edit is stated in the instruction: “Stuffing the paper into the cup”..

node_traces.evidence: Support 1 is unresolved, so completion is not established. Support 2 establishes that the paper has been moved partly into the matched cup, showing progress without completion. Therefore the requested outcome is partially fulfilled.

dependencies.evidence: The source paper and cup are visible, but the edited image shows a hand holding a blue printed item near a round object. The source paper and cup cannot be reliably matched to these objects, so whether the paper was stuffed into the cup cannot be established.

The source shows a white paper and a blue cup. In the edited image, the paper has been moved over and partly into the matched cup, showing progress toward stuffing it, but it is not visibly stuffed inside.
